subject: MAP: Benchmarking roadmap + multi-region routing & failover tests
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: MAP: Benchmarking roadmap + multi-region routing & failover tests

Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our conversation, I put together a proposed Mutual Action Plan (attached) that folds the performance benchmarking plan into the MAP so we can keep timelines and acceptance criteria aligned with procurement. High-level items:

- Objective: validate production inference economics and reliability across US/EU/APAC with multi-region routing and automated failover.
- Key metrics: p50/p95 latency (ms), TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), supported concurrency (clients/sessions), and failover time (region-to-region).
- Target acceptance thresholds (proposal):
  - US (east): p95 <= 120 ms, TTFT <= 60 ms, sustained throughput 200k tokens/min at concurrency 250
  - EU (west): p95 <= 160 ms, TTFT <= 80 ms
  - APAC (sg): p95 <= 200 ms, TTFT <= 120 ms
  - Failover: cold-region takeover within 30s (automated routing), degraded <2x latency multiplier acceptable during failover window.
- Test plan overview: baseline (no-routing) -> steady-state multi-region routing -> simulated regional outage / failover -> ramp/cold-start tests. Each run: 30m steady state after 5m warmup; repeat 3x.
- Models & configs: run both 7B quantized and 13B quantized/int8 variants (we'll list exact builds in the tech appendix).
- Deliverables & timeline: MAP milestone (sign-off) -> test window (week of Feb 8) -> results deck within 3 business days -> follow-up architecture session.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx, benchmark-script.sh, test-matrix.csv.

Can you confirm the acceptance thresholds above and whether Feb 8 works for your NOC and procurement? If APAC preference for timing, we can shift by a week.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acmecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 11:02 AM GMT
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking roadmap + multi-region routing & failover tests

Rishi —

Appreciate the quick turn. The thresholds look reasonable as a starting point; a couple of asks from our side:

1) Can you clarify the concurrency model? Are you simulating N concurrent sessions each sending streaming tokens, or N parallel independent requests? We need to validate against our client library behaviors.
2) For failover SLOs, what constitutes "cold-region takeover" — DNS TTL change, LB re-route, or application-level fallback? We want to ensure the right operations folks are on the call.

Procurement is willing to lock the Feb 8 window but would prefer if the APAC testing happens during their business hours (SG time) — could we split the test: US/EU on Feb 8, APAC on Feb 15?

I'll loop in procurement and our NOC once we finalize the MAP.

—Tom
Tom Hayes
Head of Platform Partnerships | Acme Cloud
tom.hayes@acmecloud.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 21, 2026 at 10:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking roadmap + multi-region routing & failover tests

Team —

Quick tech notes to include in the MAP appendix (I added a short harness doc attached):

- Concurrency model: we should run two profiles — (A) session-based streaming: 250 concurrent client sessions issuing prompts that stream tokens back; (B) request-based: 1k parallel short requests (single-shot) to stress routing and LB behavior.
- Warmup: 5 minutes of prefix-only & KV warmup using typical 12 prompt vectors (we'll provide the set).
- Stability: each steady-state should be 30 minutes with 1 minute sampling intervals; collect GPU metrics (util, mem), kernel stalls, and KV cache hit rates.
- Failover test: orchestrated region kill (simulate zone/network failure) at t=+15m of steady-state; measure time to first successful response routed to fallback region and % of requests that hit 503.
- Tooling: we'll run the benchmark-script.sh (attached) which uses our telemetry endpoints (streaming traces + token-level timing).

I attached regional-latency-harness.md with run commands and sample payloads — please confirm we can run under Acme's VPC peering and that NOC can accept the short-duration traffic bursts.

Marissa Cole
Staff Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Updated MAP timeline & next steps (doc + DocuSign)

Tom / Procurement —

Thanks for the notes. Updated plan:

- Feb 8: US/EU run window (steady-state + failover).
- Feb 15: APAC runs (shifted to SG business hours per request).
- Feb 16: Results deck delivery (initial metrics + flags).
- Feb 18: Follow-up architecture session to review remediation/optimizations.

I attached an updated MAP (MAP_v1.xlsx) and included a DocuSign route for the MAP sign-off so procurement can accept the test scope and data handling terms. Once DocuSign is complete we'll provision the temporary test tokens and pre-create the routing policies for the test window.

Jonas — please confirm the model builds (7b-quant / 13b-int8) are available in the test pools and that we have a perf tag for repeatability. Laura — I'll need you to own coordination with Acme's SRE on the exact time-of-day for the APAC window.

Rishi
